title: Computers enable discoveries beyond working out mathematical equations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Computers enable discoveries beyond working out mathematical equations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Computers are not limited to computing the consequences of mathematical equations; directly studying the behavior of even the simplest computer programs yields fundamental scientific discoveries.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: computers are not just limited to working out consequences of mathematical equations. And indeed, what we have seen in this chapter is that there are fundamental discoveries that can be made if one just studies directly the behavior of even some of the very simplest computer programs.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “Why These Discoveries Were Not Made Before” (from p. 42), p. 45. Scope: the role of computers in basic science

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-13: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The negative limitation is refuted by numerous directly inspectable program explorations, and novel regularities are reproducible. Whether discoveries are fundamental is evaluative, but the substantive capability claim is resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run non-equation-defined programs and document novel, reproducible regularities in their outputs that were not obtained by solving traditional equations. Explicit examples confirm that computers support this broader mode of scientific discovery.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Fundamental is a historical value judgment rather than a quantitative property.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: That a computer can iterate a rule other than a traditional equation is built into the notion of a program. Calling the resulting findings fundamental discoveries adds an evaluation that no dataset separates from the rival evaluation that they are recreational mathematics. The sentence is methodological rhetoric.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim says that studying simple programs yields fundamental scientific discoveries and that computers are not confined to evaluating equations. 'Fundamental' is an evaluative label, and once it is removed the remainder is close to a description of what computation is.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fundamental is an honorific without a confirming measurement.

Whether a mathematical finding about programs counts as a scientific discovery is a classificatory dispute.
